blockers.description: WORKTREE RESCUE MUST USE `git diff --cached`, NOT `git diff`. When 22-05 was killed by the spend limit, its pending work was STAGED (git status --short showed `A `). Plain `git diff` returned 0 bytes and `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` returned nothing, so the insurance patch was EMPTY while 52 KB across 10 files sat in the index. Acting on that empty patch would have silently destroyed real work on worktree removal.
blockers.workaround: On any worktree rescue: read `git status --short` first. `A ` means staged. Capture with `git diff --cached`, and additionally take a physical `cp -r` of new directories. Verify the patch is non-empty before trusting it.

blockers.description: STATE.md state verbs corrupt the file. `state.begin-phase` fired again this session exactly as the prior handoff predicted: three U+2014 em dashes into an ASCII-only public repo, plus first-line-only replacement of two multi-line body fields orphaning both tails mid-sentence. Its own JSON reported only four tidy field updates.
blockers.workaround: Snapshot to scratchpad, run the verb ONCE, diff against the snapshot, repair by hand, then assert `LC_ALL=C rg -c -N '[^\x00-\x7F]' .planning/STATE.md` (exit 1 = zero matches = clean). Never trust the verb's report; the diff is the evidence. NOTE: roadmap.update-plan-progress was clean both times this session.

blockers.description: worktree.cleanup-wave reports ok=false with `worktree_remove_failed -- is not a working tree` for the LAST-completing agent in each wave. Happened in BOTH waves. The MERGE succeeds; only the already-reaped directory's removal fails, which then skips the branch delete.
blockers.workaround: Cosmetic. Verify with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <each plan commit> HEAD` before concluding anything is lost, then `git worktree prune`, `git branch -d <branch>` (safe -d refuses if unmerged -- a free check), and rmdir the empty directory.

decisions.decision: 22-01 dropped the plan's owner-naming conjunct from isBareCatchAll.
decisions.rationale: As literally specified the predicate could not fail against the tracked tree. The implemented form (CATCHALL_CONDITION_RE && !isResidual, with isResidual driven by an explicit RESIDUAL_MARKER_RE) is strictly stronger AND is what D-01 actually mandates: the residual is recognized by an explicit marker, never by absence of a skill name, so a branch that merely forgets an owner FAILS. Verified in code by the orchestrator.

decisions.decision: 22-03 shipped five step-1 branches where the plan specified four.
decisions.rationale: Branch (b) could not carry both the green-step ask and the two-hop: owns() needs destinations[0] === 'lz-tpp' for c6 but the ordered pair ['lz-red','lz-tpp'] for c4, and destinationsIn() returns first-occurrence order. No single wording satisfies both. Split into (b) green-step and (c) two-hop.

decisions.decision: 22-03 moved the `See "<heading>"` pointer from the end of step 1 to its lead-in.
decisions.rationale: A trailing pointer parses INSIDE the residual branch, and those headings name sibling slugs, so the residual would report affirmed destinations and fail isDeclaredResidual(). Pointer form and heading strings are byte-identical, only relocated.

decisions.decision: 22-05 declined the plan's offered repo-root cwd for the eval suite.
decisions.rationale: `cwd = args.cwd || REPO` goes straight to the spawn. A repo-root cwd puts this phase's planning docs (which state the expected owner per case) and variant A's own SKILL.md bodies one Read away, so a variant_c session could recover exactly the sections variant C removes. Used the prompts dir instead; reasoning and residual walk-up risk recorded in suite.json's repo_note. This is an eval-integrity decision, not a style one.
